screen.channel_changed: Channel editor: changed rows marked until saved

screen.channel_name: Text entry: a channel name on the keypad
screen.channel_contact: Channel editor: picking the TX contact
screen.channel_discard: Leaving the channel editor with unsaved changes

flash.start.title: Choose a Task
flash.task.install.text: Install OpenDigitalRadio or update an existing installation.
flash.task.backup.text: Save the firmware, channels, settings and calibration to a file.
flash.task.restore.text: Restore a radio from a backup file.
flash.task.help.text: Recover a radio after a failed or incomplete installation.
flash.log.summary: The radio programming utility reports which radio and firmware you install, restore or back up, and the result, so that failures can be investigated.
flash.log.sent: Sent: a random ID, the task, the radio model, the firmware version and features, and the result or error. Never your firmware files, backups or radio data.
flash.log.kept: Stored with your IP address. Custom build requests are stored the same way even with reporting off, to stop abuse. Never sold or shared.
flash.log.choices: Opt out with ?reporting=0, or --no-reporting in odrflash.
flash.log.contact: To see or delete your data, email
flash.start.privacy: Firmware comes from this site. Your stock firmware file, backups and radio data stay on your computer.
flash.support.none: This browser cannot communicate with radios. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.usb: This browser cannot install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.support.serial: This browser cannot communicate with a radio running OpenDigitalRadio. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
flash.sim.banner: Practice mode: the radio is simulated.
flash.sim.image: Practice mode uses a made-up firmware.
flash.radio.title: Select Your Radio
flash.radio.detect_hint: If the radio already runs OpenDigitalRadio, connect it, turn it on and select Detect Radio.
flash.build.title: Select Features
flash.build.lead: Full includes every feature this radio supports. Turn individual features on or off below to create a custom build.
flash.build.unavailable: {error} You can also build the firmware yourself (see below).
flash.build.on_request: The firmware is built when you continue. This usually takes less than a minute.
flash.build.version_on_request: Version {ref} is built when you continue. This usually takes less than a minute.
flash.version.title: Version {ref}.
flash.version.text: This link installs this version instead of the latest release. Install it only if you were asked to test it.
flash.version.bad: This link requests version "{ref}", which could not be found. A version link requires a release name (for example v0.3.0) or a full 40-character commit hash. Request a new link or install the latest release.
flash.version.confirm_text: Version {ref} is not the latest release and may contain defects that the release does not. Install it only if you were asked to test it.
flash.version.confirm_back: You can return to the latest release or restore your backup at any time.
flash.build.no_image: No firmware is available. Go back one step.
flash.build.self_text: Build the firmware with this command, then select the file below.
flash.now.title: Current Firmware
flash.now.odr_text: Connect the radio and turn it on. The radio programming utility reads the installed version.
flash.now.stock_text: The firmware installed at the factory.
flash.now.unknown_text: The stock firmware file is required.
flash.now.reading_codec: Reading the voice codec from the radio…
flash.now.stock_backup_later: The radio programming utility cannot yet back up the original firmware on this radio. After the installation it backs up the channels, settings and calibration, which the installation does not change.
flash.now.stock_backup_planned: After the installation, the radio programming utility backs up the channels, settings and calibration, which the installation does not change.
flash.backup.lead: The backup is saved as a file on this computer.
flash.backup.after_lead: The radio still contains its original channels and calibration. Back them up now.
flash.backup.saved: Backup saved as “{name}” ({size} KB). Store it in a safe place.
flash.backup.incomplete: Some parts could not be read: {files}. The remaining parts were saved.
flash.backup.note_after: Created immediately after OpenDigitalRadio was installed over the original firmware, before any other change.
flash.backup.not_back: The backup is saved, but the radio has not restarted yet. Turn the radio off, then on again, and wait for the home screen before continuing.
flash.backup.task_lead: Connect the radio and turn it on with OpenDigitalRadio running.
flash.backup.add_stock: Include my stock firmware file in the backup (required to restore the original firmware)
flash.backup.stock_none: The radio programming utility cannot back up a radio that runs its original firmware. Choose Install instead; a backup is created immediately after the installation.
flash.codec.title: Voice Codec
flash.codec.lead: DMR voice requires the radio manufacturer's voice codec. The codec is not part of OpenDigitalRadio; it remains in the radio or is taken from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.mode.keep: Keep the codec in the radio
flash.codec.mode.merge: Use the codec from my stock firmware file
flash.codec.key_from_radio: The radio's update key was read from the radio.
flash.codec.stock_unknown: not a recognized stock firmware file
flash.write.title: Install
flash.win.title: Windows: install the update-mode driver (once per computer)
flash.win.failed: On Windows, this usually means the update-mode driver is not installed. Install it, then try again:
flash.win.step1: Download and run Zadig (no installation required):
flash.win.step2: Put the radio in update mode (see above) and connect it.
flash.win.step3: In the Zadig device list, select “{product}”. The USB ID fields show {usb_id}. If it is not listed, choose Options › List All Devices.
flash.win.step4: Choose WinUSB as the driver (right of the green arrow) and click Install Driver, or Replace Driver. Wait until Zadig says it succeeded.
flash.win.step5: Disconnect the radio, put it back in update mode and try again.
flash.win.note: Only update mode needs this driver. Other tools that use the same USB device, such as the maker's upgrade tool or the MD-380's CPS, need their own driver back. To restore it, uninstall the device in Device Manager with “Delete the driver software”, then plug the radio in again.
flash.write.unexpected: The radio reports “{what}”, which does not match this model. Verify that you selected the correct radio.
flash.write.failed: The installation stopped ({error}). Put the radio in update mode and install again.
flash.f4.codec_text: This update is installed over the cable and leaves the voice codec in the radio. No stock file and no update mode are required.
flash.f4.title: Install
flash.f4.lead: Keep the radio on and connected until the radio programming utility reports completion. The screen does not change during the installation.
flash.f4.safety: If the installation is interrupted, the radio starts in update mode the next time it is turned on, and the installation can be completed there.
flash.f4.enter_failed: The radio did not start the installation: {error}. Nothing was changed. Use update mode below instead.
flash.f4.after_fail: If the radio no longer responds, turn it off and on. It starts in update mode, and the installation can be completed below.
flash.f4.repick: The radio reconnected on a new port. Select it again to continue.
flash.f4.kept: Part of the codec shares a flash area with the firmware. That area was saved as {file} first, and the codec is written back unchanged.
flash.f4.ok: Installation complete and verified. The radio restarts.
flash.f4.same: The radio already has this firmware. The radio restarts.
flash.done.title: Verify Installation
flash.done.lead: The radio restarts. When the screen is on again, verify the installation.
flash.help.calm_text: The radio programming utility never writes the part of the radio that runs update mode, so update mode remains available. From update mode, the radio can be restored to OpenDigitalRadio, to your backup or to its original firmware.
flash.help.s.dark: Radio does not turn on, or the screen stays dark
flash.help.s.dark_text: No display, or no response at all.
flash.help.s.stuck: Radio turns on but does not work correctly
flash.help.s.stuck_text: It freezes, restarts repeatedly or shows unexpected content.
flash.help.s.stopped_text: An error, a disconnected cable or a computer that went to sleep.
flash.help.s.novoice_text: FM works, but digital calls are silent.
flash.help.s.channels_text: Channels, contacts or settings are missing or changed.
flash.help.s.revert_text: Restore your backup or the original firmware.
flash.help.battery_text: A discharged battery is the most common cause. Install a charged battery, or charge this one for an hour, then turn the radio on.
flash.help.um_lead: Update mode works even when the firmware is damaged. Put the radio in update mode; the radio programming utility then confirms that it can reach the radio.
flash.help.um_not_found: The radio programming utility did not find the radio in update mode. Try the following, then select Check again:
flash.help.hint_cable: Insert the cable fully into the radio, and try another USB port.
flash.help.hint_keys: Hold the keys before you turn the radio on, and keep holding them until it is on.
flash.help.nohope_lead: The cause is usually the battery or the cable.
flash.help.nohope_battery: Charge the battery fully, or try another battery.
flash.help.nohope_port: Try another cable or another computer, if available.
flash.help.ask: If the problem persists, report it on the issue tracker:
flash.help.fine_text: The radio is not damaged. Choose a recovery option.
flash.help.c7_reach: The radio programming utility can reach the radio over the cable when it is turned on, even if the screen stays dark.
flash.help.fix.again_text: No files required. Recommended when an installation was interrupted.
flash.help.fix.backup_text: Requires the backup file created by the radio programming utility (.zip).
flash.help.fix.backup_channels: Requires the backup file created by the radio programming utility (.zip). Only the channels and settings are restored.
flash.help.fix.stock_c7: Requires the backup the radio programming utility created before the first installation.
flash.help.fix.iap_text: No files required. Use when the radio does not start and the other options cannot reach it. No backup is taken.
flash.help.fixed_text: If the problem returns, open Troubleshooting again.
flash.help.stock_done_text: The radio restarts with its original firmware. Channels and calibration were not changed.
flash.done.ready: OpenDigitalRadio is running and DMR voice is available.
flash.done.no_codec: The radio has no voice codec, so DMR voice is not available; FM works. Go back to the codec step and use the codec from your stock firmware file.
flash.restore.title: Select Backup File
flash.restore.lead: Select the .zip file that was saved when the radio was backed up.
flash.restore.to_odr_text: The firmware and codec as backed up, followed by the channels and settings.
flash.restore.to_stock_text: The manufacturer's firmware from your stock file, including the codec.
flash.restore.stock_needed: Select your stock firmware file. It contains the original firmware and the key that update mode requires.
flash.restore.done_fw: The radio restarts with the firmware from the backup. The backup contains no channels or settings, so those are unchanged.
flash.restore.done_stock: The radio restarts with its original firmware.
flash.restore.spi_note: Channels and calibration were not changed. To restore the original channels, use the manufacturer's programming software.
flash.restore.codeplug_lead: When the radio has restarted, connect it. The radio programming utility compares its channels and settings with the backup and writes back the differences.
flash.restore.codeplug_refused: The radio rejected {n} of {total} parts (protected areas).
flash.err.load: The radio programming utility did not load completely. Reload the page.
flash.err.security: The browser blocked USB access. Open the radio programming utility over HTTPS.
flash.err.no_serial: This browser cannot communicate with the radio. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_usb: This browser cannot install firmware. Use Chrome or Edge.
flash.err.no_answer: The radio did not respond. Verify that it is on and running OpenDigitalRadio, and close any other program that uses the radio.
flash.err.wrong_board: The radio reports that it is a {board}, not a {name}.
flash.err.not_in_bootloader: The radio is not in update mode.
flash.err.need_stock_for_key: Select your stock firmware file first. The radio programming utility requires it to unlock update mode.
flash.err.stock_as_image: That is a stock firmware file, not an OpenDigitalRadio image.
flash.net.found: The radio is in USB network mode, so the radio programming utility cannot communicate with it.
flash.net.none: No radio found. Check the cable, and verify that the radio is on and running OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.net.step1: On the radio: Tools > USB network (OK, 5, 4), choose “Switch USB to serial”.
flash.net.step2: If Settings > Connections > USB network at start is on, turn it off, or the radio starts as a network adapter again.
home.codec: The AMBE voice codec isn't included. The installer keeps the one in your radio or takes it from your stock firmware file.
home.f_voice_text: DMR Tier II and FM. CTCSS/DCS, VOX, scan, dual watch, VFO.
home.f_data_text: Text messages, location (LRRP, ARS), emergency, call alert, radio check.
home.f_network_text: MMDVM hotspot, single frequency repeater, APRS. Over USB: status page, rigctld, SNMP, TFTP.
radio.note.dm1701: FM, DMR voice and data, text messages, the hotspot and the USB network services work on air.
radio.note.dm32: FM and DMR voice, CTCSS/DCS, APRS and GPS work on a radio. FM transmit deviation and an outdoor GPS fix are still being checked.
radio.note.md380: Has run on a radio and is in testing. No CTCSS/DCS yet.
radio.note.dm1801pro: FM with CTCSS/DCS, DMR voice and data, text messages, the hotspot and single frequency repeating work on a radio. VHF transmit and VOX are still being checked.
radio.note.db25d: Bring-up, not for general use: FM receive and transmit work, DMR is a build option that is not finished. Installation reads the original firmware first.
planned.note.tyt-md-uv380--md-uv390-rete: Same hardware family as the DM-1701. Next in line.
planned.note.tyt-md-9600-retevis-rt90: Mobile radio, same hardware family as the DM-1701.
planned.note.radioddity-gd-77-tyt-md-760: Needs a radio for development. A DM-1801 bought new today is not v1.
flash.build.needs: Requires {names}, which is enabled with it.
flash.backup.opt.all_text: Firmware, codec, calibration, codeplug and the rest of the memory chip, including the stock firmware's resources.
flash.backup.opt.firmware_text: The firmware memory (firmware and codec) and the factory calibration.
flash.backup.opt.codeplug_text: Channels, contacts, zones and settings, and the factory calibration.
flash.codec.need_key: The radio programming utility requires it to unlock update mode.
flash.codec.need_codec: The codec is taken from your stock firmware file.
flash.codec.key_saved: This browser remembers the radio's update key.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio: The codec was read from the radio and verified. This browser keeps a copy, so an interrupted installation can still be completed.
flash.codec.codec_from_radio_unsaved: The codec was read from the radio and verified. This browser cannot keep a copy (for example in a private window), so an interrupted installation requires the stock firmware file.
flash.codec.codec_saved: The codec this browser saved from your radio earlier is written back.
flash.codec.or_connect: If the radio already runs OpenDigitalRadio, go back and select it. The radio programming utility then verifies the codec in the radio.
flash.codec.anyway_text: To use the codec from your stock file anyway, select the file, then choose “Use the codec from my stock firmware file” below.
flash.restore.to_codeplug_text: The channels, contacts and settings as backed up. The firmware is not changed.
flash.build.untested: OpenDigitalRadio is still in development on the {name}. For testers only: back up the radio first and keep your stock firmware file.
flash.build.wrong_options: The firmware was built without {name}={value}. Try again.
flash.err.wrong_option: The radio reports that it is an {board}, so its {option} is {value}. Go back to the build step and select that option.
flash.sim.try_c7000: Practice with a DM-1801 Pro (original firmware)
radio.c7_step1: Connect the programming cable to the radio and to the computer.
radio.c7_step2: Open the radio programming utility and choose the cable. A radio that already runs OpenDigitalRadio is detected without holding keys or turning it off.
radio.c7_step3: Otherwise, turn the radio off and on again when prompted. Do not hold any keys. The screen stays dark and the LED on top blinks orange while the radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.retry_safe: The part of the radio that runs update mode is never written, so the radio can always be connected again.
flash.c7.retry_how: Try again. If the radio programming utility cannot reach the radio, turn it off, select Back, and turn it on when prompted. An interrupted installation resumes where it stopped.
flash.c7.bundle_note: program-memory.bin holds the radio's firmware and codec (1 MB). data-memory.bin holds the channels, contacts, settings and factory calibration (16 MB). Without it, original-channels.bin holds the start of that memory with the original channels, and calibration.bin is the factory calibration page.
flash.c7.visual.cable: The radio can be on or off at this point.
flash.c7.visual.cycle: Turn the radio off, then on again with the power knob.
flash.c7.visual.led_wait: LED: slow orange blink. The radio is in update mode and waiting.
flash.c7.visual.led_busy: LED: fast orange blink. Transfer in progress; do not touch the radio or the cable.
flash.c7.visual.screen_off: Screen: dark, as expected in update mode.
flash.c7.visual.screen_loader: Screen: "PC Loader Connected". The keys are inactive until the radio restarts.
flash.c7.visual.screen_on: Screen: on. The radio is running normally.
flash.c7.connect.title: Connect Your {name}
flash.c7.connect.step_cable: Connect the programming cable to the radio's speaker-microphone jack and to this computer. Use a charged battery.
flash.c7.connect.step_choose: Select Choose Cable, then select the cable in the list the browser shows.
flash.c7.connect.which_port_text: Disconnect and reconnect the cable while the list is open; the entry that disappears and returns is the cable. It is often named FTDI, CH340, CP210x or PL2303, "usbserial" on a Mac, or COM followed by a number on Windows.
flash.c7.connect.odr_loading: Switching the radio to update mode. Do not touch the radio. The screen shows "PC Loader Connected" shortly.
flash.c7.connect.odr_failed: The radio did not switch to update mode ({error}). Turn it off and on instead.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart: The radio programming utility restarts the radio to enter update mode. This takes a few seconds.
flash.c7.connect.odr_restart_failed: The restart did not enter update mode. Turn the radio off and on instead:
flash.c7.connect.step_on: Turn it on again. The radio programming utility is waiting and connects within a second.
flash.c7.connect.no_keys: Do not hold any keys. In update mode the screen stays dark and the LED on top blinks orange slowly.
flash.c7.connect.hint_order: Turn it off and on again. The radio programming utility is waiting now.
flash.c7.connect.hint_plug: Insert the cable plug fully into the radio. A loose plug is the most common cause.
flash.c7.connect.hint_battery: Use a charged battery. With a weak battery the radio may not enter update mode.
flash.c7.connect.hint_ch340: This cable uses a CH340 chip. Some of these cables cannot reach update mode. If the radio is still not found, use a cable with an FTDI chip.
flash.c7.connect.no_rom: The radio did not respond within three minutes.
flash.c7.connect.load_failed: Preparing the radio failed ({error}). Turn it off and try again.
flash.c7.connect.found_stub: The radio is still in update mode from the previous session.
flash.c7.connect.found_odr_stub: The radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.connect.found_rom: The radio is in update mode.
flash.c7.connect.led_rom: The LED on top of the radio blinks orange slowly and the screen is dark. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.led_odr: The radio's screen shows "PC Loader Connected" and the LED on top blinks orange slowly. Continuing…
flash.c7.connect.wrong_radio: This firmware is for the {name}, but the connected radio is a {other}. Nothing was written. Start over and select the {other}.
flash.c7.check.title: Back Up and Verify the Radio
flash.c7.check.lead_first: Before the installation, the radio programming utility backs up the radio's firmware memory. This backup is required to restore the original firmware, and it contains the voice codec that OpenDigitalRadio uses. It is downloaded and also kept in this browser.
flash.c7.check.lead_update: The radio runs OpenDigitalRadio, so the radio programming utility only verifies the codec, which takes a few seconds. A full backup is optional.
flash.c7.check.only_copy: This backup is the only copy of your radio's original firmware.
flash.c7.check.only_copy_text: The manufacturer does not offer this firmware for download. Store the file in a safe place, such as cloud storage or a USB drive. Without it, the original firmware cannot be restored.
flash.c7.check.opt_progmem_first: Required before the first installation. Contains the original firmware and its codec.
flash.c7.check.opt_cal_text: The radio's factory tuning, read together with the original channels stored next to it. Together with the firmware memory, this restores the radio to its factory state.
flash.c7.check.cal_missing: not found at the expected location. The area that should contain it was saved.
flash.c7.check.opt_q128_text: Channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration. The radio programming utility never changes these, but a copy is recommended.
flash.c7.check.progmem_skipped: not required (only the codec was read)
flash.c7.check.saved_both: downloaded as “{name}” and kept in this browser
flash.c7.check.saved_download: downloaded as “{name}” (this browser cannot keep a copy, for example in a private window)
flash.c7.check.saved_slot: the codec is kept in this browser
flash.c7.codec.keep: The radio's codec is intact and is kept.
flash.c7.codec.from_image: The codec is taken from your firmware file.
flash.c7.codec.from_radio: The codec from the radio's original firmware (version {tag}) is transferred.
flash.c7.codec.from_browser: The codec this browser saved from this radio is transferred.
flash.c7.codec.from_file: The codec is taken from your file {name}.
flash.c7.codec.none: No codec. FM works; DMR voice is not available.
flash.c7.codec.action: DMR voice requires the radio's own codec
flash.c7.codec.action_text: The radio programming utility found no recognized codec in the radio. Select a firmware backup of this radio (program-memory.bin from an earlier backup) or a stock firmware file.
flash.c7.codec.without: Install without the codec (FM only; the codec can be added later)
flash.c7.codec.none_risk: DMR voice is not available until the radio is reinstalled with a codec.
flash.c7.write.title: Install
flash.c7.write.careful: Do not disconnect the radio or the cable until the radio programming utility reports completion.
flash.c7.write.careful_text: The LED blinks fast during the installation. Only changed parts are written, and each one is verified. If the installation is interrupted, run it again.
flash.c7.write.ok: Installation complete and verified. The radio restarts.
flash.c7.write.map_label: The radio's firmware memory, one square per part
flash.c7.done.lead: The radio programming utility queries the installed firmware over the same cable.
flash.c7.done.ready: OpenDigitalRadio is running. FM and DMR voice are available.
flash.c7.done.no_codec: OpenDigitalRadio is running without a codec, so DMR voice is not available. Reinstall with a codec.
flash.c7.done.no_answer: The radio has restarted but does not respond over the cable yet. Turn the radio off, then on again, wait for the home screen and select Check Again.
flash.c7.done.backup_kept: Keep the backup you downloaded. Restore, on the start page, uses it to restore the original firmware.
flash.c7.done.backup_kept_odr: Keep the backup you downloaded. Restore, on the start page, uses it to return the radio to the firmware it ran before this update.
flash.c7.done.next_time: Future updates switch the radio to update mode automatically; turning it off is not required.
flash.c7.done.next_time_power: For future updates, the radio programming utility tries to switch the radio to update mode automatically, and asks you to turn it off and on only if that fails.
flash.c7.backup.lead: Works with any firmware on the radio. Every part is verified after it is read.
flash.c7.backup.q128_text: The whole data memory: channels, contacts, settings and the factory calibration.
flash.c7.backup.cal_missing: The factory calibration was not found at the expected location. The backup contains the area that should hold it.
flash.c7.restore.title: Restore Firmware
flash.c7.restore.lead: Writes the backup's firmware and codec back exactly. Only the parts that differ are written. The start-up area is never written.
flash.c7.restore.done: Restore complete and verified. The radio restarts with the restored firmware.
flash.c7.restore.other_radio: This backup is from another radio model.
flash.c7.restore.data_note: The radio programming utility does not write the data memory back. The radio keeps its current channels and settings.
flash.db25d.stock.found: The radio is running its original firmware.
flash.db25d.stock.lead: The radio programming utility switches the radio to update mode through the diagnostic console of the original firmware. This takes about {min} minutes. Nothing is written to the radio's memory in this step; the backup and the installation follow once the radio is in update mode.
flash.db25d.stock.note: Keep this page open and do not touch the radio. The radio stops responding to its keys and the screen stops changing until the installation is finished or the radio is turned off and on.
flash.db25d.stock.stopped: Stopped. The original firmware is still running. Select Search Again to start over.
flash.db25d.stock.writing: Preparing update mode: transferring, about {min} min remaining
flash.db25d.stock.verifying: Preparing update mode: checking, about {min} min remaining
flash.db25d.stock.retry_how: Turn the radio off and on, wait until it has started, then select Search Again. Nothing in the radio's memory was changed.
flash.db25d.stock.unknown_build: This version of the original firmware is not supported for switching to update mode.
flash.db25d.stock.unknown_how: Supported versions are 909E.DBB.EARSAB.018 and .020. The radio can still be installed through the factory update mode, but no backup of the original firmware is taken that way.
flash.db25d.stock.no_answer: the radio did not respond after the switch
flash.db25d.stock.no_stub: The radio did not enter update mode ({error}). Nothing in the radio's memory was changed.
flash.db25d.stock.no_stub_off: Turn the radio off. If it does not turn off, remove the battery for a few seconds.
flash.db25d.stock.no_stub_on: Turn it on, wait until it has started, then select Search Again.
flash.db25d.stock.found_stub: The radio is in update mode.
flash.db25d.stock.led: The radio no longer responds to its keys; this is expected in update mode. Continuing…
flash.db25d.none.lead: The radio did not answer. Check the following.
flash.db25d.none.on: The radio is on and the programming cable is connected to it and to this computer.
flash.db25d.none.cable: The cable plug is fully inserted. A loose plug is the most common cause.
flash.db25d.none.stock: If the radio does not start, or the other options do not reach it, use the factory update mode: select Use Factory Update Mode.
flash.db25d.none.odr: If the radio runs OpenDigitalRadio but does not answer, select Recover at Power-On, then turn the radio off and on.
flash.db25d.check.opt_progmem_text: The firmware, the codec and the factory calibration copy. Required before the first installation.
flash.db25d.check.lead_iap: The radio is reached through the factory update mode, so it was not read and no backup of its current firmware is taken. If you have a backup from an earlier installation, keep it.
flash.db25d.check.is_stock_other: the original firmware, a version without a codec recipe (included in your backup)
flash.db25d.codec.action_text: The radio programming utility found no recognized codec in the radio. Firmware version 909E.DBB.EARSAB.020 is not supported yet. Select a DB25-D PRO stock firmware file of version 018 (2024-05-09 or later) from the manufacturer. The codec in it works on every firmware version.
flash.db25d.iap.lead: The radio installs through the factory update mode of its original loader. The loader itself is never written.
flash.db25d.iap.step_go: Select Install. The radio programming utility then listens for the radio.
flash.db25d.iap.careful_text: The screen stays blank during the installation, which takes several minutes. The radio turns itself on in OpenDigitalRadio when it is finished.
flash.db25d.iap.listening: Listening for the radio. Enter the factory update mode now.
flash.db25d.iap.ok: Installation complete and verified. The radio starts OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.db25d.iap.cancelled: Cancelled. Nothing is changed before the radio reports the factory update mode.
flash.db25d.iap.retry_safe: The loader in the radio is never written, so the radio can always enter the factory update mode again.
flash.db25d.iap.retry_how: Select Try Again, then turn the radio off and enter the factory update mode again.
flash.db25d.iap.restore_lead: The backup's firmware and codec are written through the factory update mode of the radio's original loader. The loader itself is never written.
flash.db25d.iap.restore_step_go: Select Restore. The radio programming utility then listens for the radio.
flash.db25d.iap.restored: Restore complete and verified. The radio starts the restored firmware.
flash.db25d.iap.restored_text: The radio restarts with the firmware from the backup. Channels and settings in the radio's memory were not changed.
flash.db25d.bundle_note: program-memory.bin holds the radio's whole program memory: the firmware, the codec and the factory calibration copy. The channels and contacts in the radio's NAND memory are not part of this backup.
